entities.name: CUBN
observations: Cubilin; literature search found no primary study establishing direct cooperation with EGFR to cause cell detachment. This negative search result does not prove interaction is impossible.

entities.name: EGFR
observations: No identified primary mechanistic evidence in the reviewed searches showed CUBN-dependent EGFR signaling or cooperative induction of detachment.

PMID:27495374 reports EGFR cooperating with CDCP1 in cell detachment and adherens-junction disruption through Src-dependent EGFR transactivation; this is distinct from the earlier CUBN/cubilin evidence.

entities.name: PMID:23592779
observations: Cases et al. (2013) reported Cubn binding to FGF8 and a role in FGF-pathway signaling and developmental cell-survival phenotypes; this study does not establish EGFR-dependent detachment.

entities.name: PMID:18448595
observations: In HK-2 proximal-tubule cells, CUBN/megalin knockdown reduced light-chain uptake and light-chain-induced EMT/morphological changes; this does not demonstrate EGFR cooperation or detachment.

entities.name: CDCP1
observations: CUB domain-containing protein 1 (CDCP1; also called SIMA) is distinct from CUBN/cubilin. PMID:27495374 reports CDCP1 and EGFR cooperation in breast cancer cell detachment and adherens-junction disruption.

In MDA-MB-468 cells, CDCP1 expression promoted detachment and suspension growth; phosphorylation-site mutant Y734F did not support suspension growth similarly. The study reports a CDCP1–Src–EGFR complex and Src-dependent EGFR transactivation. Results were cell-context dependent.

entities.name: PMID:27495374
observations: Primary 2016 report titled “CUB domain-containing protein 1 and the epidermal growth factor receptor cooperate to induce cell detachment.” In breast cancer models, CDCP1 and EGFR cooperated in detachment and adherens-junction disruption; reported mechanism involved CDCP1–Src–EGFR signaling.
Retrieved evidence identifies MDA-MB-468 cells and CDCP1 Y734F mutant; response was not universal across tested cell backgrounds.

entities.name: CDCP1-EGFR detachment
observations: A primary study (PMID:27495374) reports that CDCP1 and EGFR cooperate to induce breast cancer cell detachment and adherens-junction disruption, with a CDCP1–Src–EGFR signaling complex; evidence is cell-context dependent.
